scores.thoughts: The bill addresses FERC licensing timelines for hydropower projects but contains no provisions related to federal appropriations, budgets, or expenditures. It is purely regulatory in nature.
No provisions in the bill address tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection.
The bill has no connection to healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services.
No relevance to firearms regulation or Second Amendment issues.
The legislation does not touch on immigration, visas, or border policy.
No provisions related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill concerns civilian hydropower licensing and has no bearing on military or defense budgets.

While hydropower is a form of renewable energy, the bill only extends administrative deadlines for already-licensed projects. It neither expands environmental protections nor limits regulations; any environmental effects are incidental and not the purpose of the legislation.
No provisions affect welfare programs, food assistance, or social services.
The bill has no relation to schools, education funding, or school choice.
No connection to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance regulation.
The legislation does not address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions on tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
The bill does not authorize spending or address deficit reduction.
No relevance to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The bill contains no foreign aid or international assistance provisions.
No connection to voting rights, election administration, or voter ID.
The legislation does not address technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance.
No provisions related to labor rights, unions, or workplace regulations.
The bill does not engage with religious exemptions or anti-discrimination law.
